deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform is allowed to destroy the firewall rule. Deleting a rule silently removes the traffic controls it enforced, so a policy should require PREVENT to block accidental or unreviewed removal of network protections.

description.description:
An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when
you create the resource.
description.rationale: Free-text description of the firewall rule shown in the console and API. It is documentation only and has no effect on which traffic is permitted, so there is no secure value to enforce.

destination_ranges.description:
If destination ranges are specified, the firewall will apply only to
traffic that has destination IP address in these ranges. These ranges
must be expressed in CIDR format. IPv4 or IPv6 ranges are supported.
destination_ranges.rationale: Lists the destination CIDR ranges the rule applies to. Network address ranges are a team addressing choice reflecting their own network design, and per the assessment guidance range sizing is not a platform policy target.

direction.description:
Direction of traffic to which this firewall applies; default is
INGRESS. Note: For INGRESS traffic, one of 'source_ranges',
'source_tags' or 'source_service_accounts' is required. Possible values: ["INGRESS", "EGRESS"]
direction.rationale: Selects whether the rule applies to inbound or outbound traffic. Neither value is inherently insecure; it is a functional choice about what the rule is for, so there is no direction a platform policy should mandate.

disabled.description:
Denotes whether the firewall rule is disabled, i.e not applied to the
network it is associated with. When set to true, the firewall rule is
not enforced and the network behaves as if it did not exist. If this
is unspecified, the firewall rule will be enabled.
disabled.rationale: Turns the firewall rule off without deleting it, so the traffic controls it defines stop applying while the resource still appears to exist. A policy should require it to be false so rules are not silently deactivated.

enable_logging.description: This field denotes whether to enable logging for a particular firewall rule. If logging is enabled, logs will be exported to Stackdriver.
enable_logging.rationale: Controls whether connections matched by this rule are logged. Without logging there is no record of what traffic the rule permitted or blocked, so a policy should require it to be enabled for auditability and incident investigation.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: Identifier assigned to the firewall rule. We do not constrain what teams name their resources; the name has no bearing on the traffic the rule allows or denies.

network.description: The name or self_link of the network to attach this firewall to.
network.rationale: Reference to the VPC network the firewall rule attaches to. We secure the referenced network through its own policies rather than constraining which network a team points a rule at.

priority.description:
Priority for this rule. This is an integer between 0 and 65535, both
inclusive. When not specified, the value assumed is 1000. Relative
priorities determine precedence of conflicting rules. Lower value of
priority implies higher precedence (eg, a rule with priority 0 has
higher precedence than a rule with priority 1). DENY rules take
precedence over ALLOW rules having equal priority.
priority.rationale: An integer that sets the order in which this rule is evaluated against others in the same network, with lower numbers taking precedence. It is an ordering mechanism rather than an access control: it decides which rule wins a conflict, not what traffic is permitted. The correct number depends entirely on the team's surrounding rule set.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the project the firewall rule belongs to. This is a reference to where the resource lives rather than a configurable security control, and a platform policy cannot assume any specific project.

source_ranges.description:
If source ranges are specified, the firewall will apply only to
traffic that has source IP address in these ranges. These ranges must
be expressed in CIDR format. One or both of sourceRanges and
sourceTags may be set. If both properties are set, the firewall will
apply to traffic that has source IP address within sourceRanges OR the
source IP that belongs to a tag listed in the sourceTags property. The
connection does not need to match both properties for the firewall to
apply. IPv4 or IPv6 ranges are supported. For INGRESS traffic, one of
'source_ranges', 'source_tags' or 'source_service_accounts' is required.
source_ranges.rationale: Lists the source CIDR ranges the rule applies to. As with destination ranges, address ranges are team addressing decisions that vary per deployment, so a generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain them.

source_service_accounts.description:
If source service accounts are specified, the firewall will apply only
to traffic originating from an instance with a service account in this
list. Source service accounts cannot be used to control traffic to an
instance's external IP address because service accounts are associated
with an instance, not an IP address. sourceRanges can be set at the
same time as sourceServiceAccounts. If both are set, the firewall will
apply to traffic that has source IP address within sourceRanges OR the
source IP belongs to an instance with service account listed in
sourceServiceAccount. The connection does not need to match both
properties for the firewall to apply. sourceServiceAccounts cannot be
used at the same time as sourceTags or targetTags. For INGRESS traffic,
one of 'source_ranges', 'source_tags' or 'source_service_accounts' is required.
source_service_accounts.rationale: Selects source instances by the service account they run as, as an alternative to source tags. It is used here to identify which instances the rule matches, not to grant or restrict any permission, and the accounts referenced are team-specific.

source_tags.description:
If source tags are specified, the firewall will apply only to traffic
with source IP that belongs to a tag listed in source tags. Source
tags cannot be used to control traffic to an instance's external IP
address. Because tags are associated with an instance, not an IP
address. One or both of sourceRanges and sourceTags may be set. If
both properties are set, the firewall will apply to traffic that has
source IP address within sourceRanges OR the source IP that belongs to
a tag listed in the sourceTags property. The connection does not need
to match both properties for the firewall to apply. For INGRESS traffic,
one of 'source_ranges', 'source_tags' or 'source_service_accounts' is required.
source_tags.rationale: Selects source instances by network tag so the rule applies to traffic from them. The tags a team uses to group their own instances are a naming and architecture choice specific to their deployment, so a generic policy cannot say which tags belong here.

target_service_accounts.description:
A list of service accounts indicating sets of instances located in the
network that may make network connections as specified in allowed[].
targetServiceAccounts cannot be used at the same time as targetTags or
sourceTags. If neither targetServiceAccounts nor targetTags are
specified, the firewall rule applies to all instances on the specified
network.
target_service_accounts.rationale: Selects which instances the rule applies to by the service account they run as. As with target tags, this scopes the rule to part of the team's fleet and references accounts a platform policy cannot know in advance.

target_tags.description:
A list of instance tags indicating sets of instances located in the
network that may make network connections as specified in allowed[].
If no targetTags are specified, the firewall rule applies to all
instances on the specified network.
target_tags.rationale: Selects which instances the rule applies to by network tag. This scopes the rule to part of the team's fleet rather than configuring any security control on the rule itself, and the tag names are specific to each deployment.

allow.description:
The list of ALLOW rules specified by this firewall. Each rule
specifies a protocol and port-range tuple that describes a permitted
connection.

allow.ports.description:
An optional list of ports to which this rule applies. This field
is only applicable for UDP or TCP protocol. Each entry must be
either an integer or a range. If not specified, this rule
applies to connections through any port.

Example inputs include: [22], [80, 443], and
["12345-12349"].
allow.ports.rationale: Lists the ports the allow rule applies to. A port number alone does not determine who can reach the service; exposure depends on the source ranges paired with it, which are themselves a team addressing choice. Which ports a workload legitimately needs open varies entirely by application, so there is no set a generic policy could mandate.

allow.protocol.description:
The IP protocol to which this rule applies. The protocol type is
required when creating a firewall rule. This value can either be
one of the following well known protocol strings (tcp, udp,
icmp, esp, ah, sctp, ipip, all), or the IP protocol number.
allow.protocol.rationale: Sets which IP protocol the allow rule covers. The protocol a rule targets follows from what the workload actually runs, and no single protocol is more secure than another in isolation, so this is a functional choice rather than a security control.

deny.description:
The list of DENY rules specified by this firewall. Each rule specifies
a protocol and port-range tuple that describes a denied connection.

deny.ports.description:
An optional list of ports to which this rule applies. This field
is only applicable for UDP or TCP protocol. Each entry must be
either an integer or a range. If not specified, this rule
applies to connections through any port.

Example inputs include: [22], [80, 443], and
["12345-12349"].
deny.ports.rationale: Lists the ports the deny rule applies to. Denying traffic restricts rather than exposes, so there is no insecure value here for a policy to block.

deny.protocol.description:
The IP protocol to which this rule applies. The protocol type is
required when creating a firewall rule. This value can either be
one of the following well known protocol strings (tcp, udp,
icmp, esp, ah, sctp, ipip, all), or the IP protocol number.
deny.protocol.rationale: Sets which IP protocol the deny rule covers. As with deny ports, this narrows what is permitted rather than widening it, so no value weakens the security posture.

log_config.description:
This field denotes the logging options for a particular firewall rule.
If defined, logging is enabled, and logs will be exported to Cloud Logging.

log_config.metadata.description: This field denotes whether to include or exclude metadata for firewall logs. Possible values: ["EXCLUDE_ALL_METADATA", "INCLUDE_ALL_METADATA"]
log_config.metadata.rationale: Determines how much detail is captured in firewall logs. Including metadata gives investigators the context needed to trace a connection, so a policy should require the more complete option rather than the stripped-down one.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the firewall. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456. The field is ignored when empty.
The field is immutable and causes resource replacement when mutated. This field is only
set at create time and modifying this field after creation will trigger recreation.
To apply tags to an existing resource, see the google_tags_tag_binding resource.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Binds resource manager tags to the firewall at creation time. The params block is passed with the API request but is not persisted as part of the resource payload, so the values never appear in the Terraform plan and cannot be evaluated. Which tags a team applies is also specific to their own org hierarchy.
